text: Access and security - Publisher reports persistent insecurity keeping several Ituri control points non-functional and disrupting one of 15 Ituri laboratories (14 active, 93%); too few teams and IPC supplies in some Ituri zones, a strike in one zone and insecurity in two others; low reception capacity at four Ituri treatment sites; too few treatment sites and limited specialty products in Tshopo; work still needed on one Haut-Uele treatment centre and on nutrients for specific diets; one functional testing device and sample storage conditions in Nord-Ubangi; missing IPC-trained staff, emergency kits and waste infrastructure in Sud-Ubangi, with weak community data reporting, unpaid community relays and a provider strike; Nord-Kivu care data completeness of 79% with three zones missing; and 9 Bas-Uele suspects leaving isolation without authorisation before a laboratory result. The security section reports missing isolation equipment and basic material at several Sud-Kivu control points and no formal sanitary barriers at some Haut-Uele control points. IPC counts: Nord-Kivu 12 of 29 rings opened, 16 of 20 health facilities and 13 of 28 households decontaminated; Ituri 35 rings opened, 25 households and 16 health facilities decontaminated; Haut-Uele 4 rings opened (printed with an opening rate of 75%, which no whole number of rings gives for 4), 4 households and 1 facility. No intervention effect is established.
